title: A Photographic Look at Sputnik 1, the Satellite That Launched the Space Age 69 Years Ago - Nautilus
gist: The USSR's Sputnik 1, launched October 4, 1957 from Baikonur, was the first human-made object to reach and stay in orbit — a leap no one outside the Soviet Union, including the U.S., expected, which triggered the political, military and scientific race culminating beyond the 1969 moon landing.

insights.claim: The USSR's Sputnik 1, launched October 4, 1957 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in present-day Kazakhstan, was the first human-made object to reach space and stay in orbit.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Historical anchor for the space economy's origin.
insights.locator: There have been many milestones of note

insights.claim: Sputnik 1 was only a 23-inch-diameter metal sphere, yet the rush of political, military and scientific developments up to and beyond the 1969 moon landing can be traced back to it.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Shows how a single technological surprise can catalyze decades of state spending — a template for today's AI and space races.
